```{r, include = FALSE}
# figures as WebP: lossless (the same pixels as PNG in about half the space), or lossy at quality 90 when that is
# less than half the size; any failure of magick keeps the PNG
webp <- function(path) {
  tryCatch(
      {
        if (!requireNamespace("magick", quietly = TRUE) || !isTRUE(magick::magick_config()$webp)) return(path)
        img <- magick::image_read(path = path)
        out <- sub(pattern = "[.]png$", replacement = ".webp", x = path)
        tmp <- tempfile(fileext = ".webp")
        magick::image_write(
            image   = img
          , path    = out
          , format  = "webp"
          , quality = 100
          , defines = c(`webp:lossless` = "true")
          )
        magick::image_write(image = img, path = tmp, format = "webp", quality = 90)
        if (file.size(tmp) < file.size(out) / 2) file.copy(from = tmp, to = out, overwrite = TRUE)
        unlink(c(path, tmp))
        out
      }
    , error = function(e) path
    )
}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = FALSE, comment = "", fig.path = "man/figures/README-", dpi = 120,
                      dev = "ragg_png", fig.process = webp)
```

enc   <- function(x) {
  x <- gsub("-", "--", x, fixed = TRUE)
  for (p in list(c(" ", "%20"), c("(", "%28"), c(")", "%29"), c(">", "%3E"), c("=", "%3D"), c("+", "%2B"), c("|", "%7C"))) {

}

## Overview

**baystability** fits the linear-bilinear models of multi-environment trials, AMMI and SREG (GGE), by the general
Bayesian method of Perez-Elizalde, Jarquin and Crossa (2012). The data of an earlier trial with the same genotypes and
environments can be the prior: its cell means, effects and singular value decomposition give conjugate normal and
von Mises-Fisher priors, weighted by its replicates. Every parameter has a posterior distribution, and the biplot
carries highest posterior density (HPD) regions.

* `bayes_ammi()`: the Gibbs sampler (compiled), with `.prior_data` (an earlier trial as prior), `.model = "AMMI"` or
  `"SREG"`, the number of terms, chains, burn-in and a seed; summaries with HPD intervals, diagnostics, DIC and
  WAIC;
* `bayes_gge()`: the SREG (GGE) model, the same as `bayes_ammi(.model = "SREG")`;
* `bayes_ammi_biplot()`, `bayes_gge_biplot()`: the biplots with HPD regions;
* `bys_compare()`: WAIC and DIC of several fits; `bys_interpret()`: a plain-language interpretation;
  `bys_cite()`: the references of a result;
* `bys_ls_means()`, `bys_ls_ge_effects()`, `bys_ls_ammi()` and the other `bys_ls_` functions: the tables and the
  least-squares AMMI (the names of version 0.2.0 still work, with a deprecation warning);
* `bys_app()`: all of this in a web browser, without code.

Version 1.0.0 replaces the sampler of version 0.2.0. That version read the earlier trial from objects in the
workspace, never sampled the singular values and returned a precision computed from a residual that was never
updated (see NEWS). The new sampler reproduces the 38 linear effects of Table B.1 of the paper to within 0.03
posterior standard deviations. It adds exact two-column moves, without which the genotype scores of a fit with all
terms cannot move.

For Bayesian stability analysis in general (Finlay-Wilkinson, Eberhart-Russell and Shukla models, stability indices,
probabilities of superior performance), see **bayesstability**. For the Bayesian AMMI model of Crossa et al.
(2011), see **bayesammi**.

## Installation

```r
install.packages("baystability")
```

## Quick start

```{r quick, fig.width = 9, fig.height = 5.5}
library(baystability)
data(cultivo2008)
data(cultivo2009)
fm <-
  bayes_ammi(
      .data       = cultivo2009
    , .y          = y
    , .gen        = entry
    , .env        = site
    , .rep        = rep
    , .nIter      = 3000
    , .prior_data = cultivo2008
    , .n0         = NULL
    , .model      = "AMMI"
    , .k          = NULL
    , .burnin     = 1000
    , .thin       = 1
    , .chains     = 2
    , .priors     = bys_priors(
          mu_mean     = 0
        , mu_var      = 1e+8
        , tau_mean    = 0
        , tau_var     = 1e+8
        , delta_mean  = 0
        , delta_var   = 1e+8
        , lambda_mean = 0
        , lambda_var  = 1e+8
        , nu          = 1
        , s2          = NULL
        )
    , .level      = 0.95
    , .seed       = 2012
    , .align      = TRUE
    , .waic       = TRUE
    )
fm$summary[block %in% c("mu", "sigma2", "lambda")][1:5]
bp <-
  bayes_ammi_biplot(
      fit           = fm
    , burnin        = 0
    , thin          = 1
    , pb            = c(0.10, 0.05)
    , plot_stable   = FALSE
    , plot_unstable = TRUE
    , ncolors       = 5
    , .which        = "both"
    , .grid         = 100
    )
bp$biplot
```

* References of the methods behind a result: `bys_cite()`
